author: Elagood89
title: ABSOLUTE DISGRACE AND SHAMBLES OF A COMPANY!
review: Read the bad reviews before thinking about using Yell, they are 100% accurate. Yell are only interested in signing you up to a business to business contract that you cannot get out of. They are not interested in growing your business. It all sounded great when I was contacted by one of their reps and lots of promises were made about how using their service would boost our rankings on Google and get us calls. They promised that their own site and the directories they add you to appear top in Google search results and this is why we weren't getting found. This is not the case. What they don't tell you is that there is no cooling off period and the contract can only be cancelled before the confirmation email is received. It was not possible for me to read the T&C's because I was still on the phone with the rep who also sent the confirmation email at the same time! In their T&C's it clearly states that a contract can only be cancelled if notified in writing before the confirmation email is received. I didn't have that opportunity because MY RIGHTS WERE DENIED TO ME. After realising that I also had been mis-sold many of the features once I had access to the reputation manager dashboard, I spoke to one of their account managers who told me that I had no option but to continue with the 12 month contract. I then contacted their customer service team to express that the services I signed up for were generating zero calls and VERY little traffic. On contacting the customer helpline I was faced with abuse and treated appallingly by their representatives. On top of this I was called by another sales rep advising that our advert couldn’t be given the correct category unless we paid MORE money, something else I wasn’t told from the beginning. They sell you the earth and deliver nothing. It’s an outdated platform, with very good sales people taking advantage of small businesses / sole traders. I have since spoken to many small businesses in my network who have had a similar experience, including my solicitor!!! As well as being in the press recently highlighting their underhanded tactics to rip off small businesses it's not looking good for them. Worst company I have ever dealt with, full stop.

title: Total con don’t use. I’m not wasting my money with them next year!
review: I’ve been with checkatrade since 2014 and have the highest amount of good reviews in my area. When I first joined checkatrade it was about getting the best tradesmen with high reviews and they would be shown first to potential customers. Now it’s all changed so the more money you pay the more exposure you get so the good tradesmen don’t get shown. Every job is shown to 3 tradesmen and the customer isn’t shown the qualified and best tradesmen automatically. Checkatrade has been sold many times and lost its way and now just about squeezing as much money out of the tradesmen as possible. I’ve known a lot of local experienced tradesmen quit through the sham practices who’s been with them for many years. Years ago you could have multiple skills listings and postcodes for nothing extra and now you get charged for each heading and postcode! You could end up paying £1000’s per month. In 2022 I had 82 profile views in a month and 55 quality leads may 2026 I got 2 leads and they didn’t reply! DON’T WASTE YOUR MONEY. Next year I’m gone!

They will try and charge you for so many different revenues of advertising, and now also pay for leads on top of your membership fee which is 3k a year. review: I signed up with Checkatrade expecting a steady flow of quality leads, but my experience has been very disappointing. I was not clearly told at the start that leads are shared with multiple traders (up to three). This makes it much harder to win work and significantly reduces the value of the service. I’ve been paying £490 per month, and over three months I’ve only secured one job worth £150. On top of that, many of the leads I receive don’t respond at all. When I try calling, a lot of them go straight to voicemail, which raises serious concerns about the quality and validity of the leads. Overall, the service has not delivered what was expected based on the sales process. I would strongly advise others to fully understand how the lead system works before committing to a contract.

Whenever there’s an issue you can never get through to anyone and if you do it’s to a call centre in a different country where you will struggle to communicate with the operator on the other end. The only time they call you is when they’re trying to sell you some extra you ca add to your membership. When your contract is nearly up you then have the task of trying to cancel your membership (which if I was you I would). They give you two weeks to do this and they won’t reply to emails or answer the phone to let you cancel the “automatic renewal “ as they call it. What they refer to as an automatic renewal is actually them doubling your monthly payments and putting you on a completely different plan because they’ll tell you they no longer offer the plan you originally took out a year before, so in my eyes that isn’t a “contract renewal” as the original contract you take out is never ever the same as the one they force you into the second year. The aggressive marketing techniques they use over the phone are diabolical, please do yourself a favour and stay well clear of this company there are so many other company’s that offer a better service, by far the worst out of all the advertising company’s I’ve used.

author: UK Business Owner
title: “Serious Concerns About the Authenticity of Bark Leads”
review: I created an account on Bark because I was interested in using the platform to find customers for my services. However, before purchasing any credits, I decided to carefully examine how the platform actually works. After monitoring the platform for a while, I have reached the conclusion that I simply do not have enough confidence in what is being presented to me to spend any money on it. The app consistently shows me around 178 “matching leads”, yet when I check the map and try to see the actual jobs available in my area, I can only see around 15. So my question is very simple: where are the rest of the 178 leads? Furthermore, I have noticed that many of the same requests appear day after day. From the perspective of a business being asked to purchase credits simply to access contact details, this raises some serious questions. Bark does not guarantee me a customer or even a job. Essentially, I am being asked to pay for access to someone’s contact details, after which I still have to contact that person and find out whether they still need the service, whether they have already found someone else, whether they are still interested, and whether they will even respond to me. So what exactly am I paying for? Based on what I have observed, I have even started to question whether all of these leads genuinely represent real people who have actually requested these services. I am not claiming that Bark creates fake leads, but what I am seeing on the platform gives me reason to have this concern, and I would like a clear explanation from you. I would like to know how you verify that each lead comes from a real person, how you verify that the request is still active, and why the number of “matching leads” displayed is so different from what I can actually see on the map. This is precisely why I have not purchased any credits, and I do not intend to purchase any until Bark can provide a transparent explanation and give me confidence that the leads you are charging businesses to access genuinely come from real people who are actively looking for those services.

title: ONE STAR - after several years of business and 5* reviews on platform
review: ⭐ One star — expensive leads, poor support and account restricted without proper evidence I had used Bark for several years through one business account. I later changed the email address on that same account to reflect a change in my business branding. Bark suddenly restricted my account, claiming that I had multiple accounts. I explained clearly that I had only one account and asked them to identify the alleged duplicate. They provided no account details or evidence. Instead, I received a generic message saying the matter had been escalated to another team. Th happened at a critical time and cost me an important business opportunity. A platform selling business leads should investigate properly before removing a professional’s access. I have also found Bark leads expensive for the value received. Professionals pay upfront simply to access contact information, but Bark’s own policy says credits are normally not returned when the customer does not respond or hires someone else. Even when a return is approved, the customer receives platform credits rather than their money back. This puts most of the financial risk on the small business purchasing the lead. Their published information also appears inconsistent. The Help Centre currently says credit-return requests can be made within 14 days, while the formal terms state seven days. Credits can expire, and Bark’s terms allow credit prices to be changed at its discretion. After years as a customer, I expected a proper explanation, evidence and a prompt resolution—not an unsupported allegation followed by a generic response. Based on the high cost of leads, limited financial protection and the way my account was handled, I cannot recommend Bark to other small businesses.

On multiple occasions I’ve responded within seconds of receiving a lead. Bark even shows that I was the first professional to respond, yet I still receive messages saying the customer has already found someone. If that’s the case, the lead should never have been sold in the first place. What makes this even more frustrating is Bark’s credit refund policy. They advertise credit returns, but in reality they’ll often only refund credits if the customer never responds at all. If a customer replies saying they’ve already hired someone before the lead was uploaded, Bark still expects professionals to absorb the cost. That’s not a genuine business opportunity—it’s a wasted credit. As a small business owner, every pound matters. Paying for leads that were effectively dead before I even had a chance is incredibly disappointing and feels unfair. Bark needs to review how quickly leads are published and rethink its refund policy. If a customer has already hired someone before professionals have a realistic chance to quote, those credits should be refunded automatically. Until this issue is addressed, I can’t recommend Bark to other businesses. It has cost me money without providing the fair opportunities I paid for. Consider these facts before putting your hard earned money into bark

I called up to explain that I’d already paid full price and not actually got hired at all. I assumed that they give me extra credits or refund me the difference or something. Especially seen as though I was a new professional using their business model. I phoned up and spoke to a chap that told me that I wasn’t covered under this “hire guarantee” as I paid with Apple Pay? Makes absolutely no sense to me and they never bothered trying to keep me so that will be the last time I use this service. Do yourself a favour and don’t bother with this. I wish I’d saved my money and promoted myself with my traditional ways. You live and learn I guess. There are a lot of dead end leads on the site and time wasters,but you can get your credits refunded if the number doesn’t connect or if you can get confirmation from the lead (in a text) that they are not looking for a professional on Bark. Plus you just have to approach it from a sales perspective, it’s a numbers game and if you keep trying you will find a serious enquiry. Plus you get a ‘Get Hired’ guarantee on your first credit pack. If you purchase a large credit pack you can normally secure at least 1-2 customers if you offer a good service. As an example last week I purchased £146 worth of Credits,I found two clients with that pack the first who signed up for 10 sessions worth £350 and the other who is training twice per week paying £80 per week. But meanwhile Bark still get paid: They received their cash up front when you bought your original credits. Next up Bark message you about a limited offer on a bulk buy of credits. It seems great so you buy a load. So you hang onto your credits, saving them for better commissions. Then Bark start spamming you to use your credits. Then Bark tell you you need to upgrade to a paid profile to get noticed! Something they never originally mentioned. So you upgrade. What happens? Occasional clients find you and send you a message. It costs you up to double the usual number of credits to respond to these ‘direct leads’ and your message is once again ignored!! Finally, some leads cost 3 credits to respond. Others cost 8 to respond. And yet there seems no correlation between the number of credits and the value of the commission (if you ever actually won the commission!). I’m now trying to cancel my monthly payments for the paid profile (but there’s no obvious link to do this) and once I’ve used up my credits I’ll be leaving Bark for good. How can EVERY lead (except for my first) ignore EVERY response?? There’s something fishy about this.

It’s unknown how many other poor suppliers are responding, and you don’t often get a reply from the person who posts, so there’s no way of knowing if these are real enquiries, or if anyone ever gets a job. I quite quickly tired of watching my money evaporate. This needs more work on supplier charging & returns. Perhaps bark should take a lower fee for answering requests & then a % of jobs that book?? Just a suggestion.
